extracted.intended_audience: Readers in the British Islands and general readers interested in American private life (Anglophone public receptive to Whitman's travel/memoir essays)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for composing informal, veracious personal essays/travel reminiscences that portray everyday American life, local color, and democratic themes in a conversational, anecdotal voice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Off-hand gossipy letter tone
rubrics_metrics.description: If you will only take the following pages, as you do some long and gossippy letter written for you by a relative or friend travelling through distant scenes and incidents and jotting them down lazily and informally, but ever veraciously...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present the material as an informal, conversational letter — lax about formality, intimate in address — in order to remove formal or literary impediments and bring reader and writer closer together. The author explicitly asks readers to accept this tone so that the jottings read naturally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Veracity in depiction
rubrics_metrics.description: …jotting them down lazily and informally, but ever veraciously (with occasional diversion of critical thought about somebody or something,)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strive for truthful reporting of occurrences and sights; even within an informal/gossipy mode, accuracy and sincere observation are essential. Occasional critical asides are acceptable but should not undercut factualness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portray private/common individual life
rubrics_metrics.description: In the following book is a common individual New World private life, its birth and growth, its struggles for a living, its goings and comings and observations (or representative portions of them) amid the United States of America the last thirty or forty years...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on ordinary people's lives and private experience as central subject matter — birth, growth, daily struggles and small incidents — rather than only public events or statistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local color and incidental detail
rubrics_metrics.description: …the lights and shades and sights and joys and pains and sympathies common to humanity. (Examples throughout: French Market coffee and cobblers; levees, stevedores, cotton piles; precise theater audience reactions.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use vivid, sensory small-scale details and scene-pieces (food, places, costumes, sounds, crowd behavior) to ground recollections and convey place-specific atmosphere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accept unavoidable egotism / personal voice
rubrics_metrics.description: …with their varied war and peace, their local coloring, the unavoidable egotism, and the lights and shades and sights and joys and pains and sympathies common to humanity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permit and employ the author's personal presence and viewpoint; first-person reminiscence and admitted subjectivity are appropriate elements of this kind of writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize atmosphere and themes over discrete pieces
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon the whole, it is on the atmosphere they are born in, and, (I hope) give out, more than any specific piece or trait, I would care to rest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize the general mood, cultural milieu, and thematic climate rather than aiming primarily at polished, self-contained 'pieces' — let the atmosphere shape the writing and meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Democratic aim of literature
rubrics_metrics.description: I think Literature--a new, superb, democratic literature--is to be the medicine and lever, and (with Art) the chief influence in modern civilization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compose work with an eye toward accessibility and service to the broad public; literature should uplift, educate, and enfranchise the common people rather than cater to elite formalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good-will between common people as an underlying aim
rubrics_metrics.description: and that also, in the volume, as below any page of mine, anywhere, ever remains, for seen or unseen basis-phrase, GOOD-WILL BETWEEN THE COMMON PEOPLE OF ALL NATIONS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Let an ethic of sympathy and international/commonfolk good-will inform tone and content; the writing should foster human connection across communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blend anecdote with critical thought
rubrics_metrics.description: …jotting them down lazily and informally, but ever veraciously (with occasional diversion of critical thought about sombody or something,)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interweave narrative anecdotes and sketches with occasional reflective or critical commentary; short critical diversions are a legitimate part of the memoir/essay form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elevate individual idiosyncrasy / uniqueness
rubrics_metrics.description: (As in all art-utterance it was the subtle and powerful something special to the individual that really conquer'd.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When portraying artists, characters, or subjects, emphasize the peculiar, personal qualities that distinguish them — the 'something special' that makes a person or performance memorable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show energy, fire, and abandon in expression
rubrics_metrics.description: The words fire, energy, abandon, found in him unprecedented meanings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt bold, energetic language and expressive force where appropriate; vividness and emotional intensity are virtues in rendering memorable scenes and personalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include social context and audience reaction
rubrics_metrics.description: …the whole crowded auditorium, and what seeth'd in it, and flush'd from its faces and eyes…bursting forth in one of those long-kept-up tempests of hand-clapping peculiar to the Bowery…
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for the surrounding social environment — crowds, class, manners, reactions — as part of the scene; audience behavior and social composition can be treated as integral content, not mere background.

rubrics_metrics.name: Let literature build grand individuals from the masses
rubrics_metrics.description: We who, in many departments, ways, make the building up of the masses, by building up grand individuals, our shibboleth: and in brief that is the marrow of this book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame narratives and essays to show how broad social currents and common life foster outstanding individuals; use mass experience as context for exemplary personalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat public events alongside private reminiscence
rubrics_metrics.description: You have had, and have, plenty of public events and facts and general statistics of America;--in the following book is a common individual New World private life …
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance reportage of public/historical events with intimate recollections; private anecdote can illuminate and humanize larger historical narratives.
